source_receipts.captured_excerpt_text: Article 2 of Japan's Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Company Act (Act No. 101 of June 10, 1963) specifies exactly three companies: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., Nagoya Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., and Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., with their principal offices in Tokyo, Nagoya City and Osaka City respectively.

Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. identifies itself as SBIC East Japan. Corporate number 9011001030621; established 1963-11-15; headquarters Shibuya, Tokyo; operating area includes Shizuoka, Nagano, Niigata and eastward prefectures; names Nagoya and Osaka as sister companies.

Nagoya Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. identifies itself as SBIC Central Japan. Established 1963-11-18; operating area Aichi, Gifu, Mie, Toyama and Ishikawa; names Tokyo and Osaka as sister companies.

Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. identifies itself as SBIC West Japan. Established 1963-11-20; operating area Fukui, Shiga, Nara, Wakayama and westward prefectures; names Tokyo and Nagoya as sister companies.

Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. published a free seminar notice dated February 26, 2025 titled 'Generative AI (ChatGPT): Present and Future'. The notice says the speaker was a Microsoft Corporation executive officer and evangelist, who would discuss ChatGPT and demonstrate business uses. The notice does not announce an OpenAI partnership, integration or authenticated ChatGPT connection.

Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. lists a November 16, 2026 seminar in Omiya titled 'Current and Future of Generative AI', hosted by Tokyo SBIC and featuring Microsoft evangelist Nishiwaki. It is a public AI seminar, not an OpenAI partnership or product integration.

Evernorth Holdings Inc. Form 8-K, reporting the October 9, 2026 closing, states that 10,123,015 Class A shares and 2,905,659 Class C shares were issued to Advance Funding Subscribers in exchange for approximately $214.05 million cash and 600,000 XRP. The beneficial ownership table lists SBI Holdings, Inc. with 8,885,293 Class A shares (39.9% of Class A) and 2,905,659 Class C shares (9.0% of Class C). The table defines Class A as voting and Class C as non-voting.

Evernorth's October 9, 2026 Form 8-K footnote says the 8,885,293 Class A shares attributed to SBI Holdings are held by SBI Venture Fund 2023A Investment LPS, SBI Venture Fund 2023B Investment LPS, SBI PE Holdings Co., Ltd. and SBI Holdings USA, Inc.; each is controlled by or directly/indirectly managed by SBI Holdings, Inc., a Japanese corporation listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market. This footnote specifically describes the Class A shares; the Class C attribution appears in the table but is not separately itemized in that footnote.

Evernorth's October 23, 2026 Form S-1 states that investors contributed $214,049,995 in cash and 600,000 XRP under advance funding agreements; the cash was used to purchase 84,365,876 XRP, delivered in tranches through November 6, 2025. The cash-flow statement reports $214,049,995 proceeds from refundable investor advances and $214,000,000 purchase of digital assets. The figures are distinct: cash received, XRP purchased and XRP contributed in-kind.

Evernorth's October 9, 2026 closing Form 8-K states that gross cash proceeds at closing were approximately $272.6 million, consisting of approximately $224.6 million from Private Placement Investments and approximately $48.0 million released from the SPAC trust account after redemptions, before transaction expenses. This is gross company cash proceeds and is not the same as the $214.05 million advance cash specifically used to purchase XRP.

Evernorth's October 30, 2026 Form 424B3 states that a $30.0 million 4.00% Convertible Senior PIK Note was issued on October 12, 2026 to NH Investment & Securities Co. as trustee of Kyobo AIM Corporate Finance General Private Investment Trust No. 3. The filing reports $29.0 million net cash proceeds after a $1.0 million capital-markets-advisor fee. The note is senior unsecured, accrues 4.00% PIK interest and matures in 2031; proceeds are for general corporate purposes including potential XRP acquisition and XRP ecosystem activity, but no specific XRP purchase from these proceeds is verified.

Evernorth's October 23, 2026 Form S-1 states that the Company Facility limit was increased to $10.0 million on October 7, 2026 and $9.7 million had been borrowed as of that date. The borrowing represented Ripple payments to third parties on behalf of the Company and Evernorth, reclassified from related-party payables; this is operating/related-party debt, not evidence of XRP purchases.

Evernorth's October 30, 2026 Form 424B3 registers up to 5,218,935 Class A shares under the October 23 committed equity facility with CF Principal Investments LLC (Cantor). Its cover says that at the October 29 closing stock price of $14.71, full issuance could generate approximately $76.8 million gross proceeds; the document estimates up to $74.4 million net over approximately 14 months after estimated fees and expenses. Issuance is at Evernorth's discretion and subject to conditions.

The same October 30, 2026 Form 424B3 contains an internal inconsistency: the cover and multiple sections say approximately $76.8 million gross proceeds at $14.71 per share, while a Use of Proceeds summary at line 700 retains an older approximately $80.7 million figure. The detailed table shows $76.8 million at $14.71, $50.6 million at $10, $75.9 million at $15 and $101.2 million at $20. Preserve the stale $80.7 million summary as a source-internal discrepancy rather than silently selecting it.

The October 30, 2026 Evernorth 424B3 says the company may choose to sell all, some or none of up to 5,218,935 shares to Cantor; purchases are priced at 97% of VWAP subject to stated conditions. The maximum share count is 19.99% of pre-agreement Class A shares absent shareholder approval; Cantor's beneficial ownership cap is 4.99%. The $521,893.50 commitment fee is fully earned as of the purchase agreement date regardless of whether VWAP purchases are made or settled, subject to a stated true-up mechanism. No actual ELOC share purchase or XRP purchase from ELOC proceeds was verified in this run.

Opening askcoin.net redirected to a HugeDomains domain-profile page. This is an exchange listing, not evidence of a token or XRP relationship.

CoinMarketCap separately identifies Permission Coin with ticker ASK, token contracts on Base and Polygon and the Permission ecosystem. It is distinct from the Ask Coin exchange listing at askcoin.net. No XRP relationship was verified.
